content.title: About
content.content: Channa Saag is a traditional Indian dish made from spinach leaves (saag) and chickpeas (channa), seasoned with spices, ginger, garlic and tomato sauce. The dish is rich in plant protein, fiber and B‑vitamins.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Spinach is called "saag" in Indian cuisine and appears in hundreds of recipes.
Chickpeas are one of the oldest cultivated legumes, grown for more than 7,000 years.
Channa Saag is commonly served with Indian flatbreads (naan, roti) or rice.
The dish is popular among vegetarians because it provides a complete amino‑acid profile.
Traditional recipes often include mustard seeds and fenugreek for extra aroma.

items.title: Rich source of plant protein
items.content: Chickpeas deliver about 20 g of protein per 100 g, important for vegetarian diets.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: Spinach provides iron, calcium, magnesium and vitamin K, while chickpeas are high in folate and vitamin B6.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: The dish raises blood sugar slowly, making it suitable for people with diabetes.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Spinach contains carotenoids and lutein that protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chickpeas.

items.title: Oxalates in spinach
items.content: Large amounts of spinach can contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible people.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: If prepared with a lot of salt, the dish may be unsuitable for those with hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve Channa Saag hot, typically with Indian flatbread (naan, roti) or boiled rice. A squeeze of lime or a dollop of yogurt adds freshness.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the cooked dish in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. It can be frozen for up to 2 months; thaw in the fridge before reheating.
